summary: Georgia routed ninth-ranked Ole Miss 52-17 in Week 11 at Sanford Stadium in Athens, clinching a date with Alabama in the SEC Championship Game. Brock Bowers returned from TightRope surgery and scored, while Kendall Milton and Daijun Edwards led a 300-yard rushing attack. Ole Miss lost quarterback Jaxson Dart to an apparent collarbone injury late in the third quarter. The note includes a live-updates log, the score by quarter, and broadcast details.
one_line: Georgia beat No. 9 Ole Miss 52-17 on Nov. 11, 2023, to set up an SEC Championship Game against Alabama.
key_facts: Georgia beat ninth-ranked Ole Miss 52-17 in Week 11 on Saturday, Nov. 11, 2023, with kickoff at 7 p.m. ET at Sanford Stadium in Athens.
Georgia earned a date with Alabama in the SEC Championship Game in December, its third-straight trip; it lost to Alabama in 2021.
Georgia clinched the SEC East title for the third-straight time and sixth time in seven seasons after Missouri defeated Tennessee.

Brock Bowers returned 26 days after TightRope surgery, having missed two games after a high ankle sprain against Vanderbilt on Oct. 14; he had three catches for 34 yards and an 8-yard fourth-quarter touchdown.
Georgia finished with 300 rushing yards; Kendall Milton and Daijun Edwards each scored two touchdowns, and Milton set a career-high 127 rushing yards.
Quinshon Judkins scored both Ole Miss touchdowns and finished with 75 yards.

Jaxson Dart left at the end of the third quarter after a hit from two Georgia defenders, holding his collarbone; he passed for 112 yards and one interception, and Spencer Sanders replaced him and finished with 61 yards on four completions.
Carson Beck finished with 306 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, his fourth game this season with over 300 yards and at least two touchdowns.
Ole Miss top lineman Micah Pettus was ruled out with a broken foot bone sustained in practice.
Score by quarter: Ole Miss 7-7-0-3 for 17; Georgia 14-14-10-14 for 52.
Georgia's win streak was extended to 27 games.
Javon Bullard intercepted Dart for his second pick in two games; Daijahn Anthony intercepted Beck just before halftime.
Dayton Wade made a one-handed catch on a five-yard pass from Sanders.
The game aired on ESPN with Chris Fowler, Kirk Herbstreit and Holly Rowe, and streamed on the ESPN app and Fubo.
